patch.value: context-usage redeclared host-owned --author global, failing registration on pm-cli 2026.7.27

pm-cli 2026.7.27 ships GH-719: the host rejects any extension command whose flags shadow a host-owned global flag. The 'context-usage' command declared { long: "--author" }, so its registerCommand call failed and the command did not register against a real pm host. The existing test suite used the SDK testing harness but had no suite-wide guard asserting the host-owned flag invariant. Fix: drop the --author flag declaration from context-usage and read the value from ctx.global.author instead, matching the existing ctx.global.author fallback pattern already used in context-pack and context-handoff commands. Also fixed the audit:prod script which used plain 'npm audit --omit=dev' instead of the 'env -u npm_config_allow_scripts npm audit --omit=dev --ignore-scripts' form required by project-scoped installs. Added a suite-wide guard test asserting no registered command redeclares any of the nine host-owned globals. Bumped pm-cli to 2026.7.27.

value.author: pi-agent
value.text: Verified: activation probe prints failed=[] against the real pm host engine. npm test: 79/79 pass including the new suite-wide guard test asserting no command redeclares any host-owned global. release:check green end to end (typecheck, build, test, audit:prod, pack:dry-run, changelog:check). The --author flag is read from ctx.global.author in context-usage, and the example in the usage string remains valid since --author still works as a host-owned global.

value.author: codex
value.text: Correction during review: the initial fix repointed the ledger filter at pm's host-owned global --author, but that global means 'override mutation author for this invocation', not 'whose recorded usage to report'. Reusing it would silently narrow every context-usage report to the invoking agent. Replaced with a distinct --by flag preserving the filter semantics.

patch.value: Shipped and verified functionally 2026-07-28: the package installs and loads on pm-cli 2026.7.28 with failed:[] in pm health, and its commands register and execute. Closing the registration tracker.
